$schema_note: Canonical source-of-truth for Friday loop feature-flags and their loop-closing e2e tests. The prod launch files (the rust-ws-wrapper script + the TS plist) are NOT committed to this repo, so THIS file is the authoritative, CI-enforced record of which flags exist, their intended prod state, and the committed test that drives the WHOLE loop with the flag ON. Registry gap #27 — 'every prod-ON flag has a passing loop e2e test' — is enforced against this file by scripts/ci/verify-prod-flag-tests.mjs.
why_this_exists: Recurrence prevention for the L0 silently-inert-loop disaster: three loops shipped with their flags ON in prod while NO committed test drove the loop to its outcome. A hand-proof done once is not a committed, CI-run test. The MAPPING gate (scripts/ci/verify-prod-flag-tests.mjs) runs on EVERY PR and asserts the flag<->test mapping exists + resolves. It does NOT verify the live wrapper/plist actually sets these flags — that drift check is deploy-time (see deployment_critical + the docs note).
test_execution_note: All mapped e2e_test entries are Rust friday-hub tests, RUN by `cargo test --workspace` in .github/workflows/rust-core.yml (none are #[ignore]'d; no key/network needed). Caveat: rust-core.yml is pull_request-triggered but PATH-FILTERED to rust-core/** — so the loop tests run on PRs that touch rust-core/, not on every PR. The mapped tests can only break when rust-core/ changes (and then rust-core.yml runs them), so coverage is sound; but a PR that does not touch rust-core/ gets only the existence check. A future vitest mapping would instead be run by the ci.yml `test` job.

deployment_critical.note: These flags are DEPLOYMENT-CRITICAL: their prod_state below is the contract a deploy MUST honor. A deploy must set EXACTLY the flags marked prod_state=on (no more, no less) on the named process. Wrapper-flag-durability concern: the rust-ws-wrapper and the TS plist must persist these env vars across restarts; a flag silently dropped on restart re-creates the inert-loop disaster. Drift-vs-live-wrapper (does the running process actually carry the manifest's prod_state=on set?) is a DEPLOY-TIME check, OUT OF CI SCOPE — tracked as a follow-up in docs/ops/prod-flag-test-gate.md.

coverage_legend.loop-e2e: A committed, PR-CI-run test drives the WHOLE loop with the flag's behavior ON and asserts the LOOP OUTCOME (e.g. mission born, work-item CompletedWithProof, memory becomes recallable, surface events emitted+read, clarification questions returned with zero model calls). This is the standard the gate's founding promise requires.
coverage_legend.destination-only: The DESTINATION loop this flag routes into has a real loop-e2e test (mapped here), but the flag's OWN on-ramp/routing decision is NOT exercised by any PR-CI test that closes the loop end-to-end. The mapped test is real and runs every PR, but it does not read this flag. This is a REAL coverage gap, recorded honestly — not a fabricated mapping.

test_kind_note: Rust producer tests use the program-standard split-env idiom: the env read (== "1") lives in a thin public wrapper, and the loop logic is a private *_flagged(bool) inner the test drives with the bool set ON directly (avoids cross-test env races; see the test file doc comments). Mapping to those tests is legitimate — the injected bool IS the flag's semantics. The ONLY thing those tests do not exercise is the thin env-string read in the binary (hub_agent_run_server.rs / bootstrap), which is the trivial trim()=="1" parse.

flags.notes: Drives mission_intake_result_for_db_flagged(.., clarify=true, ..) on a detailed intent and asserts a Mission(Active) + WorkItem row are written (the birth). arm_c (flag-off byte-identical) and arm_d (unclassified births) are sibling proofs in the same file.

JUDGMENT: the WorkItem-status arm (work_item_status_result_for_db) shares this flag but has no by-name dispatch test of equal strength — sub-coverage gap noted in the report (the mission-lifecycle arm is the loop closure for the flag).

flags.notes: Built-but-dark (registry gap #25). The mapped test seeds, per table, an OLD-terminal row, a RECENT row, an ACTIVE/non-terminal row, a CONFIRMED-memory row, and audit_ledger rows on a real Db, runs sweep_retention with the operator-approved default windows, and asserts ONLY old-terminal rows are pruned while recent + non-terminal + confirmed-memory survive and verify_audit_chain stays clean (audit_ledger row count unchanged). Sibling storage proofs: FK-safe parent-kept-then-freed, idempotent second sweep, no-non-terminal-ever-deleted across every status, bounded-batch backlog drain, default-windows-are-approved-values.

flags.closes_loop: On a FAILOVER-WORTHY primary (deepseek) route failure (5xx/408/transport, 402 quota, 429 rate-limit), the live agent loop retries the SAME call ONCE on the fallback (claude) and FINISHES on the fallback's answer, billed truthfully to anthropic; a parse-success/400/auth/no-model primary error NEVER fails over (no double-bill, no silent substitute).
flags.notes: Built-but-dark (registry gap #26). RGG is DeepSeek-only, so both provider legs are MOCKED: the named test drives the ProviderFailoverWrapper THROUGH the real friday_hub::run_loop against a real Hub Db — a DeepSeek 402 fails over to a finishing Claude mock, the loop Finishes 'PONG', and EXACTLY ONE token_ledger row is written attributed to anthropic/api.anthropic.com (no double-bill). Sibling e2e proofs in the same file: 429 + 5xx failover, and 400-malformed → loop errors closed with NO failover + NO bill. The wrapper/classifier per-case behavior (incl. the inner-parse-error double-bill guard, auth/no-model no-failover) is pinned in src/provider_failover.rs tests; the WIRING decision (flag-off byte-identical: wrapper not constructed; flag-on-but-Claude-absent: hard boot error; the exact-'1' flag matcher) is pinned in src/runtime.rs tests (failover_flag_off_does_not_construct_wrapper_byte_identical, failover_flag_on_without_claude_is_hard_boot_error, provider_failover_flag_matcher_is_exact_one_default_off).

flags.closes_loop: At boot, reconcile orphaned in-flight WorkItems no live recovery path picks up — PASS-1: a Dispatched/HubAccepted hop a dying loop was mid-flight on (#767); PASS-2 (#24b): a ReadyToDispatch (the during-model-call rest state) / ProviderRouted / ProviderWaiting row left executing=1 with a STALE heartbeat by a process that crashed DURING the model call — advancing each to FailedTerminal + the crash_recovery_abort marker via the LEGAL state machine, while NEVER touching a not-yet-running/legit-paused/awaiting (executing=0) or slow-but-LIVE (fresh-heartbeat) row.
flags.notes: Registry gap #24 (#767, PASS-1) + #24b (this PR, PASS-2 — the COMMON mid-call crash). PANEL-BLOCK FIX: the original #24b pre-advanced the WorkItem to ProviderRouted BEFORE the model call; an adversarial panel BLOCKED that reorder for two LIVE degrades (a loop Err stranded the row at ProviderRouted not the retryable ReadyToDispatch; a pre-dispatch StorageError aborted the run before the answer persisted). The fix REVERTS to driving the binding AFTER the loop, so the during-call status is ReadyToDispatch (the additive ReadyToDispatch->FailedTerminal edge makes PASS-2 reconcile it) and an errored run stays retryable. REACHABILITY is the load-bearing proof: the mapped test seeds the genuine during-call status ReadyToDispatch, simulates a mid-model-call crash (the loop's heartbeat SET fired — executing=1+stale — but the process died before the tail clear AND before the post-loop bind) and asserts PASS-2 advances it to FailedTerminal + the crash_recovery_abort marker. END-STATE/AUDIT-IDENTICAL to pre-#24b (binding timing unchanged; only two columns no read path consults are written + the final-hop bind clears executing in the same tx): proven by the full mission_runtime/runtime/resume/surface-event suites staying green. Degrade fixes are pinned: errored_mission_bound_run_stays_ready_to_dispatch_not_stranded (degrade-1), paused_run_with_swallowed_tail_clear_is_not_pass2_reconciled (degrade-3 — atomic final-hop clear; the cardinal-sin guard), long_multi_step_turn_keeps_a_fresh_heartbeat_and_is_not_reconciled + real_transport_bounds_a_hung_request_with_a_wall_clock_timeout in friday-deepseek (degrade-4). The reconcile predicate + no-degrade boundary are pinned in tests/crash_recovery.rs: pass2_aborts_stale_executing_provider_waiting, pass2_leaves_fresh_executing_provider_waiting_untouched (the slow-but-LIVE guard — a re-set FRESH wall-clock heartbeat is NEVER aborted), pass2_leaves_legit_paused_provider_routed_untouched (executing=0 is never reconciled at any age — resume must still pick it up), pass2_disabled_when_flag_off, pass2_exactly_at_threshold_is_stale_and_reconciled (5-min boundary). The marker's SET-before-each-model-call+before-tool-exec (FRESH wall-clock) + CLEAR-at-EVERY-loop-exit + atomic-clear-on-bind is proven by loop_clears_executing_at_every_exit (Finished/Paused/Blocked) and loop_sets_executing_during_the_call_and_re_entry_re_sets_it (mid-call SET observed via a concurrent reader + loop re-entry re-set). The flag matcher (exact-'1', default-off) is flag_matcher_is_default_off_and_exact_one. #767's PASS-1 cases still pass (reconcile_aborts_only_orphans_leaves_waiting_and_terminal_untouched, reconcile_is_idempotent_second_sweep_is_a_noop).

flags.closes_loop: With the flag ON, the agent loop can dispatch the L2-1 `web_fetch` capability tool: the gate Allows it (read-only, no approval pause) and the CompositeToolExecutor runs an SSRF-guarded outbound HTTP fetch (host resolved + every IP validated + pinned, redirects re-validated, 512KB read / 100KB model-facing / 30s caps), returning the body to the model. With the flag OFF (the prod default) `web_fetch` is REFUSED at the gate-dispatch chokepoint (`web_fetch_disabled_flag_off`) before the executor — the tool is UNAVAILABLE and behavior is byte-identical to today. DARK: flipping it live enables outbound egress and is OPERATOR-GATED.
flags.notes: Built-but-dark (registry gap L2-1). NO real network — the mapped test stands up an in-process 127.0.0.1 mock HTTP server, drives gate_dispatch_with_policy_enforced(.., web_fetch_enabled=true) with a `web_fetch` RawToolCall against a real Hub Db + a real CompositeToolExecutor (FsToolExecutor + the SSRF-guarded WebFetchExecutor), and asserts the loop dispatches+Executes the fetch and returns the fetched body (HTTP 200 + body) in the ToolReceipt. SSRF is wired fail-closed before EVERY fetch incl. redirects: even with the flag ON, a web_fetch to a private/metadata target under the PRODUCTION SSRF policy is refused at the executor (web_fetch_flag_on_ssrf_blocks_private_target_at_executor). The flag-OFF arm (tool unavailable, executor never reached, byte-identical for other tools) is pinned by sibling lib.rs tests web_fetch_flag_off_refuses_tool_unavailable_executor_never_reached + web_fetch_flag_off_is_byte_identical_for_other_tools; the exact-'1' env matcher by web_fetch_enabled_from_only_literal_one_enables. The SSRF guard's per-range blocking (RFC1918/loopback/link-local/metadata/ULA + DNS-resolved + non-http) is table-tested in src/ssrf_guard.rs; the executor's GET/POST + 512KB read cap + 100KB truncation + timeout + HTML-to-text + redirect-revalidation in src/http_tools.rs (all mock-server, no real net).

flags.closes_loop: With the flag ON, the agent loop can dispatch the L2-2 `web_search` capability tool: the gate Allows it (read-only, no approval pause) and the CompositeToolExecutor runs a multi-provider web search (serper/tavily via API key from env; duckduckgo/google_news_rss keyless), returning the result snippets (title/URL/snippet) to the model — it never fetches the result pages. With the flag OFF (the prod default) `web_search` is REFUSED at the gate-dispatch chokepoint (`web_search_disabled_flag_off`) before the executor — the tool is UNAVAILABLE and hidden from the model menu, so behavior is byte-identical to today. DARK: flipping it live needs operator-provisioned Serper/Tavily keys for the premium providers and is OPERATOR-GATED.
flags.notes: Built-but-dark (registry gap L2-2). NO real network — the mapped test stands up an in-process 127.0.0.1 mock returning a serper JSON body, drives gate_dispatch_with_policy_enforced(.., web_search_enabled=true) with a `web_search` RawToolCall against a real Hub Db + a real CompositeToolExecutor (FsToolExecutor + SSRF-guarded WebFetchExecutor + the WebSearchExecutor whose provider endpoints are pinned to the loopback mock), and asserts the loop dispatches+Executes the search and returns the parsed snippets in the ToolReceipt. NO silent premium->keyless fallback (parity with the TS oracle): an explicitly-configured serper/tavily WITHOUT its key returns a result CARRYING the fail-closed warning (web_search_flag_on_serper_missing_key_returns_warning_not_silent_fallback), never a degrade-to-ddg; Auto mode only ever selects the KEYLESS providers when no premium key is configured. The flag-OFF arm (tool unavailable, executor never reached) is pinned by web_search_flag_off_refuses_tool_unavailable_executor_never_reached; the menu-hide byte-identical guarantee by web_search_flag_off_prompt_menu_is_byte_identical_no_web_search; the exact-'1' env matcher by web_search_enabled_from_only_literal_one_enables. The provider routing + serper/tavily JSON + duckduckgo HTML + google_news_rss XML parsers + freshness date-filtering + no-dates warning are unit-tested (mock-server / pure, no real net) in src/web_search.rs.

flags.closes_loop: With the flag ON, the agent loop can dispatch the L2-3 `image_analysis` (vision) capability tool: the gate Allows it (read-only, no approval pause) and the CompositeToolExecutor's VisionExecutor VALIDATES every image fail-closed (workspace-root-scoped local paths, SSRF-guarded http(s) image URLs, data-uri media-type image/* + base64 + decoded-size caps, image-count/total-size bounds) then delegates to the injected VisionModelClient (the Claude vision impl in prod) and returns the analysis text to the model. With the flag OFF (the prod default) `image_analysis` is REFUSED at the gate-dispatch chokepoint (`vision_disabled_flag_off`) before the executor — the tool is UNAVAILABLE and hidden from the model menu, so behavior is byte-identical to today. DARK: vision is token-EXPENSIVE; flipping it live needs an operator-provisioned vision provider key (FRIDAY_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) and is OPERATOR-GATED.
flags.notes: Built-but-dark (registry gap L2-3). NO real model/provider, NO real network — the mapped test drives gate_dispatch_with_policy_enforced(.., vision_enabled=true) with an `image_analysis` RawToolCall (prompt + a data: URI image) against a real Hub Db + a real CompositeToolExecutor (FsToolExecutor + WebFetchExecutor + WebSearchExecutor + the VisionExecutor whose VisionModelClient is the deterministic offline StubVisionClient), and asserts the loop dispatches+Executes: the executor validates the data-uri image (media-type image/* + base64 decode + size cap) and the receipt carries the stub analysis. Provider choice: Claude/Anthropic vision (the friday-vision ClaudeVisionClient over friday-anthropic's audited Messages-API transport — image content blocks {type:image, source:{type:base64,media_type,data}} + a text block); DeepSeek has no vision route (honest gap — the trait is provider-agnostic but Claude is the only real impl). The `detail` param (low/high/auto) is VALIDATED for TS parity but NOT forwarded to the Anthropic API (no image `detail` field — a documented no-op for Claude). The flag-OFF arm (tool unavailable, executor never reached) is pinned by vision_flag_off_refuses_tool_unavailable_executor_never_reached + vision_flag_off_is_byte_identical_for_other_tools; the menu-hide byte-identical guarantee by vision_flag_off_prompt_menu_is_byte_identical_no_image_analysis; the exact-'1' env matcher by vision_enabled_from_only_literal_one_enables. SECURITY (no-degrade): image-input validation is fail-closed — vision_flag_on_ssrf_blocks_private_image_url_at_executor proves an http image URL to a private/metadata target is SSRF-refused at the executor even with the flag ON; workspace-path traversal rejection, data-uri media-type/base64/size caps, file:// rejection, and missing-provider-key->warning (never silent skip) are unit-tested in src/vision_tools.rs; the Claude image-block request shape + the detail no-op + base64 round-trip are unit-tested in friday-vision (src/lib.rs).
